source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
EdgeCore's AS02 in Sterling, Virginia publishes 114 MW of IT capacity and 685,000 square feet of technical space, and it ranks fourth among the 29 Virginia facilities that disclose a megawatt figure.

The published specification stops at power and floor area. There is no rack count, no accelerator count, and no tenant list, so any equipment figure is an outside estimate applied to the megawatt number rather than a disclosure. At 40 kW per rack the 114 MW implies roughly 2,850 racks, and at 100 kW per rack roughly 1,140, but both are assumptions about density, not facts about this building. The only certification listed is LEED, which describes the building's environmental performance and says nothing about the power, cooling, or network systems that decide what compute the campus can actually run.

The more useful signal is the disclosure gap across the state. Virginia has 376 mapped facilities and only 29 publish a megawatt figure, and those 29 total 2,563.4 MW. Most of the physical buildout in Northern Virginia is therefore invisible in capacity terms, which makes a published 114 MW unusual and gives it real weight in any count of what the state can power. The 3.5 miles to Dulles and the coordinates place the campus inside the densest data center corridor in the country, but proximity is not capacity.

What this does not establish is who occupies the space or what hardware runs inside it. A power envelope of 114 MW bounds the electricity a campus can draw, not the compute it delivers, and the efficiency between those two numbers is unpublished here.
